dna.default: generator=simplex, accretion=summed - both exact no-ops, and the no-op is a SHORT-CIRCUIT rather than a formula that lands near the shipped value. _noise_type_for("simplex") returns FastNoiseLite.TYPE_SIMPLEX, the identical enum constant setup_noise assigned unconditionally at :63; _fractal_type_for("summed") returns FastNoiseLite.FRACTAL_FBM, the identical constant from :66. Nothing else in setup_noise moved - the seven property assignments run in the same order with the same arguments, and cellular_return_type is touched on the cellular rung ONLY, so at every other value that property stays at the engine default it has always had. REACH MEASURED BY READING THE MAPS, not estimated: SIX mentions in six map files by three paths, where the promotion brief carried three. Bare tokens - `voxel_noise_demo` in ISO_Introduction (interactables row 84) and Corridor_ISO_Introduction (row 76), and `marchingcubes_voxel_noise_demo` in ProceduralGenerationMarchingCubesVovelNoise (row 97). Two curation_station rosters - Curation_Bay_isosurfaces_1 and Curation_Bay_proceduralgeneration_all_9, where the token is an entry in the station's `#artifacts:` list. And one transformation swap, `voxel_noise_demo->animated_noise_explorer` in Trial_physarum_isosurfaces, which is a target NAME and not a config at all. Not one of the six names an axis key. Neither registry entry declares default_params and neither token carries a delegate, so merged_config is EMPTY at the three bare cells and GridInteractablesComponent's `if not merged_config.is_empty()` gate at :1194 means _apply_artifact_config is never called - no metadata is stamped and apply_grid_config is never reached. The two rosters do not reach it either, and for a different reason worth recording: curation_station.gd:381 tests `inst.has_method("apply_grid_config")` on the ROOT of the instantiated scene, and this scene's root carries no script, so its `{"emissive": false}` call is skipped entirely. Even if it landed, that key is in no signature and the guard would return. Zero of six rebuild, and all six render the field they have always rendered.
dna.was: Seventeen @exports - the richest export surface in the sequence - and not one of them said what the field is MADE of. generate_density_field is four lines of arithmetic: sample noise.get_noise_3d at the corner (:125), map it to (noise + 1) * 0.5 (:128), store. No shape term, no gradient, no bias, no second layer. So the picture is a level set of one FastNoiseLite object and nothing else - the sequence's purest case of a surface that is only a threshold on a field - and the two lines deciding what that object IS sat three apart as bare constants, TYPE_SIMPLEX at :63 and FRACTAL_FBM at :66, reachable from no map, no token and no inspector. apply_grid_config was the single word `pass` at :407: a config channel wired to nothing, so even the sixteen knobs that WERE exported could not be set by a placement.
dna.note: generator is SHARED, and the sharing is the whole point. FIVE artifacts already carry it with the same four values in the same order and the same default - perlin_noise (promoted 2026-07-29), noise_terrain (08-03), noise_space and shader_noise_space (08-05), alongside simplex_noise in the same bench family - and every one of their notes says the same sentence: the noise sequence is built on comparing bases, so if each artifact spells the comparison its own way there is nothing to compare. cellular, not worley, for the same reason. THE APPROVED DESIGN FOR THIS PASS PROPOSED A NEW WORD, `basis`, with five rungs (value|perlin|simplex|smooth|cells), and it was refused. A census of all 996 declared axes across the registry turned up `generator` on four tokens carrying exactly this value list; a sixth spelling of one question is precisely the fault those five notes were written to prevent. So: same word, same four rungs, same order, same default, `cells` spelled `cellular`, and `smooth` declined (see declined). What this member adds to the family is the READING and not the vocabulary - the other five displace a height or tint a wall with the basis, and this one level-sets it. Five artifacts asking one question and one of them asking it of a boundary instead of a surface is a comparison worth having; a sixth private word would have been six unrelated facts. ONE DOCUMENTED DIVERGENCE, stated rather than glossed. The cellular rung here also sets cellular_return_type = RETURN_CELL_VALUE, which the other five do not. FastNoiseLite's default is RETURN_DISTANCE, distance-to-nearest-feature, whose one-point distribution is strongly one-sided. This file's iso_level is fixed at 0.5 and :128 maps noise to (n + 1) * 0.5, so 0.5 cuts the field exactly at its own mean - a threshold chosen for a zero-mean basis. Against a one-sided field that threshold stops being a mean, and the rung would mostly move HOW MUCH of the box is solid rather than what its boundary is made of. RETURN_CELL_VALUE is a constant per Voronoi cell with mean zero, so the cut stays at the mean and the answer is a surface with no curvature anywhere in the frame: flat plates meeting at cell walls. This is the same move shader_noise_space recorded when it amplitude-matched its four bases with three scaling constants so its axis would measure structure and not exposure. TerrainGenerator.gd:90 in this same repo already pairs TYPE_CELLULAR with RETURN_CELL_VALUE. accretion is NEW - zero uses among those 996 - and the adjacency is named rather than left for the critic. `octaves` is taken SEVEN times (mc_cave and mc_inside_cave in this sequence, plus noise_space, noise_quarry, simplex_noise, marchingcubes_cave, marchingcubes_inside_cave) and it counts HOW MANY scales survive. accretion is the RULE by which they are combined, and the count is held at this scene's shipped noise_octaves = 4 on every rung - deliberately untouched, though it is one of the seventeen exports - so the two questions cannot overlap. summed = FRACTAL_FBM SHIPPED. single = FRACTAL_NONE, one octave, the frame that shows what the other three rungs are adding. ridged = FRACTAL_RIDGED, which rectifies each octave to 1 - |n|; against simplex's mean |n| of about 0.35 that puts the field's mean near +0.3 instead of 0, so the cut at 0.5 leaves a sparser solid and the extracted surface grows blades and fins instead of lobes. pingpong = FRACTAL_PING_PONG at the engine's default fractal_ping_pong_strength of 2.0, folding the range repeatedly into banded shells and likewise skewing the mean positive. THE ARITHMETIC OF THE PICTURE, written down so a small number can be told from a dead axis. frequency is the .tscn's noise_scale 0.05, so the base wavelength is 20 world units across a 32-unit chunk: 1.6 periods per axis, i.e. the frame is dominated by one octave's worth of blob about 10 units across. Sampling is 32 points over 32 units, spacing 1.032, so the fourth octave at wavelength 2.5 is resolved at only 2.4 samples per period - right at Nyquist, and contributing at a gain of 0.125. That is why accretion is expected to be the quieter of the two axes, and it is a second reason the octave count was left alone. AND THE CAVEAT THE WHOLE FAMILY SHARES, which none of the five siblings has written down: at a fixed seed, changing noise_type does not perturb one field, it draws a different one. simplex and perlin at seed 1337 are two unrelated realisations, not two renderings of one landscape. A large bite on `generator` is therefore close to guaranteed whatever the design, and the thing to read is not the mean but the CHARACTER - whether value shows the axis-aligned creases of a cubic lattice, whether cellular shows flat plates. That is true of all five siblings equally, which is exactly what makes them comparable; it is a property of the axis and not a defect in it.
dna.shares_vocabulary_with: perlin_noise, simplex_noise, noise_terrain, noise_space, shader_noise_space - `generator` is the same axis with the same four values in the same order and the same default. This is the sixth member and the first to level-set the field rather than displace a height or tint a wall with it, which is the reason to keep the word rather than coin one: if a shared vocabulary is honest, the odd member out is the interesting measurement. The single documented departure is cellular_return_type on the cellular rung, argued in `note`. `octaves`, which four of those five also carry, is NOT taken here - accretion asks a different question and the octave count is pinned so the two cannot be confused.
dna.declined: `smooth` (TYPE_SIMPLEX_SMOOTH), REFUSED, and it is the refusal that cost something. The approved design asked for it as a fifth rung and predicted it would be the weakest, closest to simplex at about 4% - 'only just over the bite floor'. It is dropped because the four-value list is a comparison instrument held in common by five artifacts, three of whose notes assert 'the same four values in the same order'; a fifth rung on one member makes that member's mean incomparable with the other four, and what it buys is the rung already predicted to be faintest. If the sweep later wants the simplex-versus-simplex-smooth distinction, it belongs to the whole family at once and not to this member alone. `basis`, REFUSED as a name - see note. num_points_per_axis (32) - the sampling resolution, and `resolution` is already this sequence's family word, held by animated_noise_explorer and by queer_marching_cave. Not taking it a third time. noise_scale (0.05) - the biggest knob by visual effect and the one this promotion was most tempted by. Refused because against a fixed 32-point lattice over a 32-unit chunk it is arithmetically the SAME ratio: chunk_size x noise_scale = 1.6 periods across the box, so halving the frequency is indistinguishable from doubling the lattice spacing. Sweeping it re-argues resolution from the other side. iso_level (0.5) - `threshold`, taken by mc_torus_sculpture. Recorded in the prose instead, because :128 maps the noise to (n + 1) * 0.5 and so 0.5 cuts the field exactly at its own mean, which is why the shipped picture is a balanced sponge with roughly equal solid and void - and why the cellular rung had to be mean-matched. noise_persistence (0.5) and noise_lacunarity (2.0) - genuine spectral properties, but both are octave-weighting parameters and would argue with accretion for the same pixels. noise_octaves (4) - `octaves`, taken seven times, and held fixed here precisely so accretion is not measured against it. glass_color, outline_color, outline_width, use_shader, generate_colliders, chunk_size - material, chrome and size. voxel_scale - exported since the file was written and read by nothing in the build path; a dead knob, not an axis, and deliberately kept out of the rebuild signature for that reason.
dna.fixture_why: THE ONE ARTIFACT OF THIS WAVE THAT WAS ALREADY SEEDED CORRECTLY, so this is a pin and not a repair. noise_seed is a real @export defaulting to 1337, the .tscn sets 1337, and setup_noise assigns noise.seed = noise_seed BEFORE generate_density_field takes its first sample. The file contains no randf, no randi and no RandomNumberGenerator in 408 lines and builds exactly one FastNoiseLite. The pin exists only so the value STAYS pinned if a map or a future bench ever passes one - without it, a seeded run and an unseeded run of `generator` would be indistinguishable in the manifest, which is the queer_marching_cave audit failure in the other direction. Written as a bare JSON number, never the string "1337", because capture_config_sweep assigns fixture values straight onto the typed int export before _ready and a typed int rejects a String. NOT PINNED and deliberately: generate_colliders stays true, its shipped value. Collision is invisible in a still, but a ConcavePolygonShape3D built in C++ from an already-computed vertex array is cheap, and pinning it false would photograph a configuration no placement uses.
dna.framing_why: Explicit at the default because it was CHECKED rather than assumed: the sibling entry's own measurements block records aabb_size 32.0 x 32.0 x 32.0 with aabb_center at the origin, which is the chunk exactly. The subject is a cube-shaped, close to isotropic volume, so the fit-by-diagonal that letterboxes flat and thin subjects is honest here and no layers = 0 anchor is needed. THE ONE THING TO WATCH, because it is an inference and not a measurement: the density field is defined everywhere in the box at every rung, so every rung SHOULD reach every face - but ridged and pingpong push the field's mean positive and could in principle pull the surface in from the faces, which an AABB-fitted camera answers by zooming, turning a change of extent into a change of apparent scale. If the sweep shows two rungs framed at visibly different magnifications, that is the cause, and the fix is an anchor mesh rather than a smaller framing number.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config was the single word `pass` at :407. It now reads the two axes against their allow-lists (an unrecognised value is DROPPED, not applied - the science_screen failure was a typo nothing in the chain refused) and rebuilds only when a signature of every value the build reads has actually moved. The signature is not a hand-listed tuple of the two axes: _signature() strings every export generate_world consumes, so the guard cannot drift out of step with the build. voxel_scale is deliberately absent from it - the export exists and nothing reads it, so including it would let a dead knob pay for a 29,791-cube re-march. The channel stays narrow on purpose: the two axes are the only keys READ, so a token naming noise_scale or iso_level still changes nothing, because widening the channel to honour keys nobody has ever sent would be a behaviour change hiding inside a promotion. ORDERING READ OFF THE CALL SITE RATHER THAN ASSUMED. GridInteractablesComponent stamps config_* metadata at :1656-1666 and calls add_child at :1220, so metadata always lands BEFORE _ready; _ready reads it through _read_dna_metadata and builds ONCE with the right values, records the signature, and the deferred apply_grid_config that follows finds the signature unchanged and returns. A `_built` flag guards the reverse order: config arriving before the first build assigns and returns, because _ready will read the new values on its way through. THE SCRIPTLESS ROOT IS NOT A FAULT AND WAS NOT 'FIXED'. The promotion brief called it a BLOCKING STRUCTURAL FAULT - voxel_noise_demo.tscn's root is a bare Node3D and VoxelNoiseMarchingCubes.gd sits on a child - and it asked for the script to be moved up. The engine was read instead of the brief, and the brief is stale. GridInteractablesComponent._apply_artifact_config falls through at :1695 to _config_holder, a breadth-first search for the first descendant that handles config, which finds the child, stamps the metadata there and calls apply_grid_config on it, all before add_child; capture_config_sweep._holder_of does the same per key for the bench; and check_dna_declarations.unreachable_roots classifies this shape as CHILD-ONLY, informational, explicitly not a fault, since e0bc97b3b. Moving the script would have been a change with a real cost and no benefit - the ROOT is where GridInteractablesComponent attaches its _RotationTimer, and this script's _exit_tree used to blanket-free every ownerless child, so the move would have newly put that timer inside the blast radius. The script therefore stayed put and the free was narrowed instead: an `_owned` array holds the two nodes this script creates (the VoxelWorld mesh and the VoxelWorldCollision body) and nothing else is ever touched, which is identical in effect today and stops being identical the moment anything attaches a helper here. clear_world also now DETACHES before queue_free, because queue_free is deferred and a rebuild adds a second node named VoxelWorld in the same frame, which Godot would silently rename to VoxelWorld2.
dna.still_note: A still is a complete account, and this is one of the few artifacts in the sequence where that needs no qualification. There is no _process, no timer, no await and no call_deferred anywhere in the file; _ready runs setup_noise, setup_marching_cubes_tables and generate_world synchronously and the mesh is finished when it returns. Both axes are resolved inside setup_noise before the first of 32,768 samples is taken and neither is re-read afterwards. Determinism is real rather than asserted: one FastNoiseLite, seeded from an export before first use, and no other source of randomness in the file. Four runs of the same rung are the same mesh. BUDGET, checked because the failure mode is a watchdog kill and not a bad picture: 32^3 = 32,768 noise samples and 31^3 = 29,791 marched cubes per tile, all in GDScript, with an Array-of-Triangle-objects intermediate. The registry's own compute field calls this artifact HEAVY. On a 16-tile sweep that is the number to watch against the 16-second stall rule, not the bite.
dna.predicted_degeneracy: PREDICTED BEFORE THE CAPTURE, and one of the two predictions deliberately DISAGREES with the approved design so the sweep can settle it - a prediction that agrees with the sweep is worth nothing. generator, closest pair: perlin x value, predicted ~30-35% of frame, i.e. nowhere near the bite floor, and the honest reading of that is that 'closest' barely means anything on this axis. Arithmetic: perlin and value sample the SAME cubic lattice at the same spacing (1 / 0.05 = 20 world units, 1.6 cells across the 32-unit chunk) and both are zero-mean, so both produce a sponge of the same characteristic blob size and roughly the same 50% solid fraction. They differ in placement, not in scale, and a pixel metric reads placement as large. cellular should be the loudest and the most obviously different - flat plates, no curvature. The part of this I am least sure of is whether `value` shows its axis-aligned creases at only 1.6 lattice cells per axis; if it does not, the value rung will read as one more unrelated sponge. accretion, closest pair: ridged x pingpong, predicted ~12% of frame. THE APPROVED DESIGN PREDICTED summed x pingpong AT ~8% AND THIS PASS DISAGREES WITH IT. Arithmetic: ridged and pingpong both rectify or fold each octave into a one-sided shape, so both fields carry a mean around +0.3 to +0.5 against summed's 0.0; after density = (n + 1) * 0.5 and the cut at 0.5, both leave a sparse thin-walled solid of roughly a quarter to a third of the volume, while summed and single both leave a balanced sponge at about a half. If the family splits that way, the design's pair is wrong and the axis is really asking 'is the octave rectified'. If summed x pingpong really is the closest, the folding is being re-sorted back into a balanced sponge by the threshold and the axis is asking 'how many scales', which would put it too close to `octaves` to keep - so this pair decides whether accretion earns its own word. Largest pair, both predictions agreeing: single x ridged. THE DEGENERACY RISK WORTH NAMING: if ridged or pingpong pushes the mean far enough that almost every corner lands on one side of 0.5, march_cube skips the cube as 'completely inside or outside' (:205) and the tile comes back near-empty - which reads exactly like an inert axis. Read the per-tile triangle count that generate_world prints at :106 BEFORE reading the bite number.
dna.kin: SIBLING DECLARATION. voxel_noise_demo (isosurfaces.json) and marchingcubes_voxel_noise_demo (randomness.json) are two registry names on ONE scene, voxel_noise_demo.tscn - another of the one-scene-many-names families this corpus keeps turning up. The axes, the values, the fixture, the framing and this entire block are copied character for character between the two entries. They MUST measure alike; if they do not, the difference is in the bench and not in the artifact. Worth noting that the second entry lives in randomness.json rather than an isosurfaces file and its own map_sequences already claims both isosurfaces and proceduralgeneration_all - so the `generator` family it now joins, which is a randomness family, is the family it was already filed with.

dna.default: intrusion=melted, period=pair - both exact no-ops, and the no-op is structural rather than arithmetic. TerrainGeneratorGyroid.gd declares no @export of its own and never did; the eight numbers this artifact has are literals inside MarchingGyroid.glsl. melted is the const triple [4.0, 0.5, 1.0], which IS the three literals that used to be written inline at MarchingGyroid.glsl:181, :190 and :197 - they were moved from the shader to a GDScript const and handed back through a uniform, so evaluate() multiplies the same snoise results by the same three floats in the same order. pair feeds periodScale 1.0 and `p * 1.0` returns the identical bit pattern for every finite float, so `dot(sin(gp), cos(gp.yzx))` receives the argument `dot(sin(p), cos(p.yzx))` always received. THE ONE HONEST CAVEAT, stated rather than glossed: the multiplier is now a uniform where it was a literal, so a driver that contracts `p += warp * 4.0` into an FMA and `p += warp * params.warpStrength` differently could differ in the last bit. Both are the same `a + b*c` expression shape, so there is no known compiler that does, but that is the exact size of the claim - not 'the bytes are proven equal', 'the same floats travel the same expression'. THIRTEEN MAP FILES place this scene under two names and NOT ONE passes a config key. gyroid_demo in 10: Gallery_ProceduralGeneration (`gyroid_demo:0:-0.5`), ISO_ShapesGallery (`gyroid_demo:0:1:0.04`), and an `exhibit_furniture#kind:floor_work#size:l#mount:gyroid_demo` in Trial_castelvecchio / grande / kanazawa / physarum / pinch_v2 / sainsbury / soane_cabinet_vista / uffizi. GyroidDemo in 3: ISO_TorusGyroid (`GyroidDemo:0:2:0.5`), Corridor_ISO_TorusGyroid and ProceduralGenerationMarchingCubesSculpture, all bare tokens. Neither registry entry declares default_params and neither token carries a delegate, so merged_config is EMPTY for the bare placements and GridInteractablesComponent's `if not merged_config.is_empty()` gate means _apply_artifact_config is never called at all - no metadata is stamped and apply_grid_config is never reached. The exhibit_furniture mounts load, instantiate and add the scene without calling it either. Zero of thirteen reach the rebuild branch.
dna.was: 24 lines: a shader path, a class name, a `_process` overridden to `pass`, a fallback sphere, and an `apply_grid_config` whose whole body was `pass` - a method that existed only so the grid's has_method() check would find something. The artifact was recorded in the audit as having ZERO exports, which is true and is not the same as having no parameters. The registry entry above promises a `gyroid minimal surface ... triply periodic implicit function`, and the pure surface has never been rendered anywhere in this corpus: the shader writes Schoen's gyroid in one line at :185 and then perturbs it three times - a domain warp, an erosion, and a thickness modulation added to the density BEFORE the isoLevel comparison - before anything is compared to a threshold. What 13 maps show is the perturbation. What the description names is the thing underneath it.
dna.note: intrusion is a NEW word. `facture` (capsule, dome, folded_strip, platonic_grabbables, triangleprofiles - cast|facet|armature|section|wear) is the nearest relative and was refused: facture asks how a thing was fabricated, which presumes a maker, and this asks how much of a mathematical object survives being written into a noise pipeline. `weather`, `provenance`, `authorship`, `derivation` and `descent` are each already held with another meaning. The rungs are the three strengths as a LADDER rather than three knobs, and they were sized on a numpy replica of evaluate() over the same 65^3 corner grid at the scene's own iso_level of 1.0, counting connected bodies: melted (4.0, 0.5, 1.0) SHIPPED shatters the lattice into 2,859 separate bodies with no period readable anywhere in the box; formula (0, 0, 0) is ONE connected body holding 100% of the solid, every unit cell identical; eroded (0, 0.5, 0) keeps the period and pits the sheets - 1,268 bodies, but 95.3% of the solid still in one piece, a lattice surviving its own wear; drifting (0, 0.5, 1.0) restores only the space-varying threshold, so sheets thicken in some regions and thin to holes in others. 1 body against 2,859 is the axis in one number. SAID PRECISELY, because the registry's own description does not and the difference is the sequence's subject: `formula` is the pure gyroid level set at THIS ARTIFACT'S threshold, g = iso_level = 1.0, not the balanced minimal surface g = 0. GyroidDemo.tscn sets iso_level 1.0 and that export is untouched here, so what formula shows is the mathematical object at the threshold somebody already chose - which is the more honest picture for a sequence whose truth line is that the boundary between inside and outside is a decision. period is also NEW. `grain` (grabbable_line and 5 others - solid|split|quartered|lattice|shell) asks how the mass inside a fixed silhouette is divided, which is close, but its five rungs cannot be built here; `unit` (diamonds), `cell` (tessellation_lattice_demo) and `pitch_space` (harmonic_distance_table) are taken with other meanings. baseScale 0.5 against chunk_scale 20 gives ~1.59 periods per axis, and the multiplier is applied ONLY to the gyroid term's coordinate - deliberately NOT to baseScale, which also feeds the warp and the erosion, so scaling it would confound the two axes. Written this way the pair is strictly orthogonal: intrusion varies what is ADDED to the field with the period held, period varies the period with the additions held. pair 1.0 SHIPPED (~1.6 periods, two half-cells reading as a pair of sheets); sheet 0.5 (~0.8 periods, less than one full cell - the picture that shows the gyroid is a SURFACE and not a lattice); lattice 2.0 (~3.2 periods, the repeat unmistakable); weave 4.0 (~6.4 periods, a fine three-way interpenetrating weave). Both axes reach the GPU by the pattern TerrainGeneratorShapes already uses for shapeId: get_params_array() calls super and appends four floats, ParamsBuffer gains four matching trailing fields. MarchingGyroid.glsl is loaded by TerrainGeneratorGyroid and by nothing else, and TerrainGeneratorGyroid is loaded by GyroidDemo.tscn and by nothing else, so the shared eleven-field prefix every other Marching*.glsl reads is untouched by construction.
dna.declined: REFUSED, `iso_level`, and the refusal is the interesting one. It is real, it is a single float, and it is the sequence's central question - where you put the threshold is the whole of what a surface IS. It is declined because on THIS artifact the thickness modulation already varies the threshold through space, so an axis over the constant would be arguing with intrusion=drifting for the same pixels; the two would measure each other. It belongs to a sibling in this sequence that has no thickness term. REFUSED, `continuous_update` (TerrainGeneratorBase:11): it re-runs the compute dispatch every frame, which is a RATE, invisible in a still by law, and on a static gyroid it changes nothing except the risk of photographing a half-built mesh. REFUSED, `noise_offset`: it walks the field's domain, which is not a different surface but a different arbitrary sample of the same one - the same travel-through-noise-space idea refused by name on animated_noise_explorer. REFUSED, `chunk_scale` and `center_position`: a size and a placement, both self-cancelling under an AABB-fitted camera. REFUSED, an axis over the marching-cubes RESOLUTION, which is the other half of this sequence's argument (`how finely the field is sampled`) and would be a fine axis - but `resolution` is a `const int` on TerrainGeneratorBase shared by ELEVEN generators, and buffer sizes are computed from it, so it is not this artifact's to open.
dna.fixture_why: Neither key is an axis and both are already the shipped default, so this is a GUARD rather than a pin - it is here because the two silent failure modes of this artifact both end in a published sheet that is a fact about the host machine. use_fallback true, or a local rendering device / SPIR-V load that fails on the capture host, drops straight into _create_fallback_mesh: a naked SphereMesh of radius 20. Sixteen frames of a smooth grey ball, both axes measuring zero, and a verdict about the GPU. THE RUN IS ONLY VALID IF THE SWEEP LOG SHOWS `TerrainGeneratorGyroid: Generation complete!` AND DOES NOT SHOW `Creating fallback sphere`. continuous_update true would keep re-dispatching under the settle. Both are written as real booleans, never as the strings `false`, because capture_config_sweep assigns fixture values straight onto the typed export before _ready and a typed bool rejects a String. NOT PINNED, and deliberately: noise_offset. The approved design asked for `noise_offset: Vector3.ZERO` and JSON cannot hold a Vector3 - capture_config_sweep._coerce only converts String to enum int and would hand a three-element Array to a typed Vector3 export, which is a worse risk than the one it guards. It does not need a pin: GyroidDemo.tscn never sets it, no map token sets it, and its declared default IS Vector3.ZERO.
dna.framing_why: Explicit at the default because it was CHECKED rather than assumed. The generated mesh fills the whole 20 m chunk and is close to isotropic, so the fit-by-diagonal that letterboxes flat and thin subjects is honest here. Verified on the numpy replica: the surface's world AABB is 20.0 x 20.0 x 20.0 m for ALL SIXTEEN combinations of the two axes, to the voxel. That also disposes of the `layers = 0` anchor the approved design asked for - it was there because intrusion=formula was expected to build a mesh of a different extent than melted and walk the camera between tiles. It does not; the field is defined everywhere in the box and every rung crosses the threshold out to every face. Adding a 20 m anchor mesh to the scene would have changed what GridInteractablesComponent._compute_local_aabb measures for all 13 placements to fix a problem that is not there.

dna.note: Every other field in this sequence is GIVEN: gyroid_demo's by a formula, animated_noise_explorer's by noise, fifteen_cases_demo's by a lookup table, metaballs' by a fixed set of sources. This one's is DEPOSITED - a hand puts material in and the extractor finds a boundary through whatever was put - so its axis is what the hand did, and no other artifact here can carry that claim. All four rungs use THE SAME SEVEN DEPOSITS: the same six radii from the generator's own fractions (0.5/0.35/0.25/0.22/0.18/0.15 of s = chunk_scale * 0.15) plus the same centre deposit at the literal 0.3. The amount of material, the threshold and the sampling do not move between rungs; only the arrangement does, which is what makes this an axis about arrangement and nothing else. stack is the shipped standing form. sweep drags the seven along one horizontal arc that rises and settles, heavy end at +x/-z tapering to -x/+z. dab pushes them to seven of the volume's eight corners, spaced so that no two extracted surfaces touch - seven separate closed surfaces where every other rung gives one, which is the honest picture of what a deposit IS before anything fuses it, and the rung that carries the claim: the extractor did not build a body, it found the boundary of what was there. heap piles them low around the floor with the top half of the box empty. WHY THE dab NUMBERS ARE NOT FREE. iso_level is 0.3 against a plain sphere SDF, so every deposit renders at radius r + 0.3 - the smallest of the seven is a 0.345 ball and the largest a 0.6 ball, inside a box of half-extent 1.0 - and opSmoothUnion at k = scale * 0.06 = 0.12 bridges any two surfaces whose gap is under k/2 = 0.06. The result, computed rather than hoped: minimum surface gap 0.073 and every other pair at 0.21 or more, so dab separates with about 20% margin on the worst pair. These numbers are tuned against the shipped volume_size 2.0 and iso_level 0.3; they scale with chunk_scale and they do NOT survive a change of iso_level. dna.note:
THE SEQUENCE'S TRUTH LINE, LITERALLY. 'Define a field, extract a surface. The boundary between inside and outside becomes geometry.' This script is the one place in the wave where the SAME field is shipped twice, once to be looked at and once to be stood inside, so an axis declared here has to mean something from both sides. You are OUTSIDE this one: the scene's camera sits at (-15, 35, 50) looking in, with a DirectionalLight3D and five torches, so the field reads as a block of rock with a top surface and a sky.

plumb - WHICH WAY IS DOWN, AND WHETHER THERE IS A DOWN AT ALL. Everything this shader knows about gravity is one line, MarchingCubes.glsl:180: `density = -(worldPos.y+100)/300 + density`. It is the ONLY anisotropic term in the file; the six octaves above it are isotropic ridged noise, which on its own has no up. That one linear bias is what makes low regions solid and high regions air - from outside, the block's top surface and its sky; from inside, the floor you stand on. plumbScale multiplies it and nothing else. bedded (1.0) SHIPPED. overturned (-1.0) flips the sign: the same noise at the same threshold with inside and outside exchanged, rock overhead and nothing under your feet. weightless (0.0) DELETES the term and leaves pure ridged noise - an isotropic sponge with no floor, no ceiling and no sky, filling the sampled box to all six faces. steep (3.0) triples the gradient so the field swings 3.0 across the 300 m box instead of 1.0 and the solid retreats into the bottom third: a slab with a rough top, a crawl space. The four values are held IDENTICAL across all four declared tokens on purpose - it is one const on one script, and holding them identical is what makes the galleries comparable frame for frame.

octaves - HOW MANY SCALES OF ROCK SURVIVE THE LATTICE, AND THIS IS THE AXIS THAT MAKES THE SIBLINGS SAY DIFFERENT THINGS. :168 opens `for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++)`; each pass halves the amplitude and doubles the frequency, with the weight feedback at :174 gating each octave by the previous one. The literal 6 is the rung. What makes it worth declaring is arithmetic the two scenes do not share. THIS token: noise_scale 13.5, chunk_scale 300.0, so samplePos = worldPos x 0.04500 and octave 0 has ~22 m features; the marching lattice samples at 300.0/64 = 4.688 m, so its Nyquist limit is 9.38 m. The six octaves measure 22.2, 11.1, 5.5, 2.8, 1.4, 0.7 m, which puts 2 of them above the limit and the rest below it. On the sibling the same six octaves land differently, and that is the finding: mc_cave resolves TWO scales of rock, mc_inside_cave resolves FOUR, from the same script, the same shader, the same rungs and the same threshold. The artifact you stand inside can resolve two more octaves than the one you look at. That is the inside/outside asymmetry as a number rather than as a description, and it is why the axis is declared on both rather than on one.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE APPROVED DESIGN, both found by redoing its arithmetic. (1) The design said the inside scene resolves ONE more octave than the outside one; by the Nyquist figures above it is TWO (octaves 0-3 against octaves 0-1). (2) The design said the sub-limit octaves are 'COMPUTED AND THEN THROWN AWAY BY THE EXTRACTOR'. They are not thrown away, they ALIAS: content finer than the sampling cell still perturbs the corner values, which still moves where interpolateVerts puts the crossing. So the sub-limit rungs are predicted to be nearly degenerate, not exactly degenerate, and a small non-zero reading there is the expected result rather than a failed prediction.

ONE MORE THING WORTH RECORDING ABOUT THE FIELD ITSELF: :170 is `snoise(samplePos) * 2 - 1` before the ridged fold, not the plain `snoise` of the usual Lague construction, so the input to `1 - abs(noise)` spans about [-3, 1] rather than [-1, 1] and the fold is off-centre. The amplitude LADDER still halves exactly (1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 0.0625, 0.03125), which is what the octave arithmetic above rests on, but the per-octave term is not bounded by 1 and the summed density is not bounded by 1.969. Any claim about an absolute density total should be read as about the ladder, not about the sum.

PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, in projected-area currency, computed by hand rather than by rasterising the scene. Read it as an order-of-magnitude claim the sweep can falsify, not as the critic's own hottest-5%-of-crop number. capture_config_sweep places its OWN camera at dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing with FOV 34, PAD 1.9, YAW 0.62, PITCH -0.26, RES 760.

CLOSEST PAIR ON plumb: bedded (1.0) vs steep (3.0), AT ABOUT 11% OF FRAME. Solid requires the ridged sum to exceed isoLevel + k(y+100)/300. At k=1 that is satisfied up to roughly y = +15 for a typical sum; at k=3 the same sum is exceeded only by about y = -60. The top of the mass drops roughly 75 m in a 300 m box shown at ~53% of frame height, and the newly-empty band is 75/300 x 53% = about 13% of frame height across the ~42% of frame width the body occupies - call it 11% once the silhouette's obliquity is taken off. The LARGEST pair should be bedded vs overturned, over 35%, since the mass moves from the bottom of the frame to the top.

CLOSEST PAIR ON octaves, AND IT IS A PREDICTION THAT THE AXIS IS PARTLY DEGENERATE ON PURPOSE: 3 vs 6, UNDER 2%. The design named that pair too, but for the wrong reason and on the wrong scope. On this token only octaves 0-1 clear the 9.38 m Nyquist limit, so rungs 2, 3 and 6 differ ONLY in octaves that alias rather than resolve - the near-degeneracy is a three-way tie among {2, 3, 6}, not a single close pair, and 3-vs-6 is merely the member of it with the smallest amplitude difference (0.125 + 0.0625 + 0.03125 = 0.219 of the ladder's 1.969, gated down further by :174). The pair that MUST move is 1 vs 6: one octave is a smooth blobby cave with no wall texture at all, predicted over 25%.

IF 3-vs-6 COMES BACK NEAR ZERO ON mc_cave AND ALIVE ON mc_inside_cave, THE AXIS HAS DONE ITS JOB AND MUST NOT BE FILED AS DEAD. The degeneracy IS the finding: it is the Nyquist limit of the extraction lattice showing up as a photograph. A dead reading on the sub-limit rungs of one token and a live one on the other is the result this axis was declared to produce.

THE RUNG THAT COULD GO WRONG IS 1, and the confound is stated rather than hidden. Dropping octaves 1-5 removes up to 0.969 of the amplitude ladder (much less after the weight gating), and against the 1/300 gradient every unit of removed sum is 300 m of horizon. So `1` will look both SMOOTHER and EMPTIER, and the two effects are not separable in a still - octaves is borrowing plumb's pixels at its bottom rung. If that dominates the tile, the low rung should come up to 2 rather than the axis being called confounded.

dna.fixture_why:
ALMOST NO FIXTURE, and it is worth saying which of the usual reasons do not apply. _ready() is not gated: TerrainGeneratorBase._ready() runs init_compute(), run_compute(), fetch_and_process_compute_data() and create_mesh() SYNCHRONOUSLY, so the artifact builds standalone on the bench with no map, no host and no config. There is no RNG and no seed to pin - the field is Ashima/stegu simplex noise, a pure function of position, and noise_offset is fixed by the .tscn at (200, -120, 150). There is no clock in the picture: params.time is declared and never referenced. And the settle window cannot catch a half-built mesh - the sweep waits two process frames plus 0.1 s, roughly 8 frames, while the base's re-dispatch needs 12 wait-frames for GPU sync and 90 more for the mesh thread before create_mesh could run again, so what is photographed is unambiguously the mesh _ready built.

ONE BENCH HAZARD THAT IS NOT A FIXTURE PROBLEM BUT MUST BE READ FROM THE LOG: _create_fallback_mesh() on this class builds a 200 m sine TUNNEL with none of the field in it. If the capture host cannot make a local RenderingDevice, or if process_mesh_data() trips its 500,000-triangle safety abort and sets num_triangles = 0, every tile is that decoy and both axes measure zero for entirely the wrong reason. THE RUN IS ONLY VALID IF THE LOG SHOWS 'Generation complete!' AND NOT 'Creating fallback'.

ONE REAL SIDE EFFECT AT ONE RUNG, stated because it is a behaviour change and not only a picture: plumb=weightless raises the solid fraction and with it the surface area, so the triangle count rises. TerrainGeneratorBase:461 skips trimesh collision above 30,000 triangles. If weightless crosses that line it is the one rung where collision is not built - a bench-only difference that no map placement can reach, since none of the four passes a config key and the shipped rung is bedded.

FIXTURE, AND IT PINS THE HAZARD NAMED ABOVE RATHER THAN A SEED. {use_fallback: false, continuous_update: false} are both already the base class's defaults and neither cave .tscn overrides either, so the pin changes NOTHING about what any placement renders - it is written as a bool, straight onto the property before _ready, per the fixture-typing rule. What it buys is that the bench cannot silently take the _create_simple_cave_mesh() path and photograph the sine tunnel instead of the field, and cannot be handed a re-dispatching artifact mid-settle. The log check still stands as the real guarantee: valid only on 'Generation complete!', never on 'Creating fallback'.

THE SEQUENCE'S TRUTH LINE, LITERALLY. 'Define a field, extract a surface. The boundary between inside and outside becomes geometry.' plumb - WHICH WAY IS DOWN, AND WHETHER THERE IS A DOWN AT ALL. Everything this shader knows about gravity is one line, MarchingCubes.glsl:180: `density = -(worldPos.y+100)/300 + density`. It is the ONLY anisotropic term in the file; the six octaves above it are isotropic ridged noise, which on its own has no up. That one linear bias is what makes low regions solid and high regions air - from outside, the block's top surface and its sky; from inside, the floor you stand on. plumbScale multiplies it and nothing else. bedded (1.0) SHIPPED. overturned (-1.0) flips the sign: the same noise at the same threshold with inside and outside exchanged, rock overhead and nothing under your feet. weightless (0.0) DELETES the term and leaves pure ridged noise - an isotropic sponge with no floor, no ceiling and no sky, filling the sampled box to all six faces. steep (3.0) triples the gradient so the field swings 3.0 across the 280 m box instead of 1.0 and the solid retreats into the bottom third: a slab with a rough top, a crawl space. The four values are held IDENTICAL across all four declared tokens on purpose - it is one const on one script, and holding them identical is what makes the galleries comparable frame for frame.

octaves - HOW MANY SCALES OF ROCK SURVIVE THE LATTICE, AND THIS IS THE AXIS THAT MAKES THE SIBLINGS SAY DIFFERENT THINGS. :168 opens `for (int i = 0; i < 6; i++)`; each pass halves the amplitude and doubles the frequency, with the weight feedback at :174 gating each octave by the previous one. The literal 6 is the rung. What makes it worth declaring is arithmetic the two scenes do not share. THIS token: noise_scale 3.8, chunk_scale 280.0, so samplePos = worldPos x 0.01357 and octave 0 has ~74 m features; the marching lattice samples at 280.0/64 = 4.375 m, so its Nyquist limit is 8.75 m. The six octaves measure 73.7, 36.9, 18.4, 9.2, 4.6, 2.3 m, which puts 4 of them above the limit and the rest below it. On the sibling the same six octaves land differently, and that is the finding: mc_cave resolves TWO scales of rock, mc_inside_cave resolves FOUR, from the same script, the same shader, the same rungs and the same threshold. The artifact you stand inside can resolve two more octaves than the one you look at. That is the inside/outside asymmetry as a number rather than as a description, and it is why the axis is declared on both rather than on one.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE APPROVED DESIGN, both found by redoing its arithmetic. (1) The design said the inside scene resolves ONE more octave than the outside one; by the Nyquist figures above it is TWO (octaves 0-3 against octaves 0-1). (2) The design said the sub-limit octaves are 'COMPUTED AND THEN THROWN AWAY BY THE EXTRACTOR'. They are not thrown away, they ALIAS: content finer than the sampling cell still perturbs the corner values, which still moves where interpolateVerts puts the crossing. So the sub-limit rungs are predicted to be nearly degenerate, not exactly degenerate, and a small non-zero reading there is the expected result rather than a failed prediction.

ONE MORE THING WORTH RECORDING ABOUT THE FIELD ITSELF: :170 is `snoise(samplePos) * 2 - 1` before the ridged fold, not the plain `snoise` of the usual Lague construction, so the input to `1 - abs(noise)` spans about [-3, 1] rather than [-1, 1] and the fold is off-centre. The amplitude LADDER still halves exactly (1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 0.0625, 0.03125), which is what the octave arithmetic above rests on, but the per-octave term is not bounded by 1 and the summed density is not bounded by 1.969. Any claim about an absolute density total should be read as about the ladder, not about the sum.

dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, in projected-area currency, computed by hand rather than by rasterising the scene. Read it as an order-of-magnitude claim the sweep can falsify, not as the critic's own hottest-5%-of-crop number. capture_config_sweep places its OWN camera at dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing with FOV 34, PAD 1.9, YAW 0.62, PITCH -0.26, RES 760.

CLOSEST PAIR ON plumb: bedded (1.0) vs steep (3.0), AT ABOUT 11% OF FRAME. Solid requires the ridged sum to exceed isoLevel + k(y+100)/300. At k=1 that is satisfied up to roughly y = +15 for a typical sum; at k=3 the same sum is exceeded only by about y = -60. The top of the mass drops roughly 75 m in a 280 m box shown at ~53% of frame height, and the newly-empty band is 75/280 x 53% = about 13% of frame height across the ~42% of frame width the body occupies - call it 11% once the silhouette's obliquity is taken off. The LARGEST pair should be bedded vs overturned, over 35%, since the mass moves from the bottom of the frame to the top.

CLOSEST PAIR ON octaves, AND IT IS A PREDICTION THAT THE AXIS IS PARTLY DEGENERATE ON PURPOSE: 3 vs 6, UNDER 2%. The design named that pair too, but for the wrong reason and on the wrong scope. On this token only octaves 0-3 clear the 8.75 m Nyquist limit, so rungs 2, 3 and 6 differ ONLY in octaves that alias rather than resolve - the near-degeneracy is a three-way tie among {2, 3, 6}, not a single close pair, and 3-vs-6 is merely the member of it with the smallest amplitude difference (0.125 + 0.0625 + 0.03125 = 0.219 of the ladder's 1.969, gated down further by :174). The pair that MUST move is 1 vs 6: one octave is a smooth blobby cave with no wall texture at all, predicted over 25%.

IF 3-vs-6 COMES BACK NEAR ZERO ON mc_cave AND ALIVE ON mc_inside_cave, THE AXIS HAS DONE ITS JOB AND MUST NOT BE FILED AS DEAD. The degeneracy IS the finding: it is the Nyquist limit of the extraction lattice showing up as a photograph. A dead reading on the sub-limit rungs of one token and a live one on the other is the result this axis was declared to produce.

THE RUNG THAT COULD GO WRONG IS 1, and the confound is stated rather than hidden. Dropping octaves 1-5 removes up to 0.969 of the amplitude ladder (much less after the weight gating), and against the 1/300 gradient every unit of removed sum is 300 m of horizon. So `1` will look both SMOOTHER and EMPTIER, and the two effects are not separable in a still - octaves is borrowing plumb's pixels at its bottom rung. If that dominates the tile, the low rung should come up to 2 rather than the axis being called confounded.

AND THE ONE NUMBER THIS TOKEN IS EXPECTED TO DISAGREE WITH ITS SIBLING ON: 3-vs-6 should be LARGER here, perhaps 4%, because octave 3 measures 9.2 m against this lattice's 8.75 m limit and so is the one sub-ladder rung that clears it. That single crossing is the whole of the inside/outside asymmetry expressed as a measurement. If both tokens return the same number for 3-vs-6, the Nyquist reading is wrong and the axis is just an amplitude ladder.

mc_inside_cave.description: GPU interior cave view — marching cubes cave seen from inside.
mc_inside_cave.name: mc_inside_cave
mc_inside_cave.qfep_connection: Standing inside the isosurface: the cave is where the field says *in*, and you are in it. The boundary wraps around the walker — geometry experienced from the wrong side of the skin.

dna.default:
interior=caverned, and it is a SHORT-CIRCUIT rather than a lookup: _cave_strength() returns the const SHIPPED_CAVE_STRENGTH = 0.4 the moment interior is `caverned` and never reaches the table at all. That const IS the literal that used to be written inline at MarchingCubesFlat.glsl:193 as `terrainDensity - (caveNoise * 0.4)`; it was moved out of the shader into a GDScript const and handed back through a uniform. GDScript's 0.4 is a float64 that PackedFloat32Array rounds to the nearest float32, and GLSL's 0.4 literal compiles to that same nearest float32 -- identical bit pattern -- so `caveNoise * params.caveStrength` multiplies the same value by the same value. THE ONE HONEST CAVEAT, stated rather than glossed, and it is gyroid_demo's caveat repeated because it is the same manoeuvre: a driver could contract `terrainDensity - caveNoise*0.4` and `terrainDensity - caveNoise*params.caveStrength` into different FMA shapes and differ in the last bit. Both are the same `a - b*c` expression, so there is no known compiler that does; the claim is 'the same floats travel the same expression', not 'the bytes are proven equal'.

REACH MEASURED, and not one of the four placements passes a config key. Under mc_flat_landscape: the bare grid cell `mc_flat_landscape` in ISO_FlatTerrain, and curation_station rosters in Corridor_ISO_FlatTerrain (`#artifacts:mc_flat_landscape,mc_overhang_landscape,mc_terrain_demo#layout:row`) and Curation_Bay_isosurfaces_1. Under the sibling token marchingcubes_flat_landscape: `marchingcubes_flat_landscape:0:-2` in ProceduralGenerationMarchingcubesFlatLandscape -- a rotation and a y-offset, not a config key. NEITHER registry entry declares default_params and neither token carries a delegate, so merged_config is empty for all four and GridInteractablesComponent's `if not merged_config.is_empty()` gate means _apply_artifact_config never runs: no metadata is stamped and the guarded rebuild is unreachable from every map that exists. All four come out bit-identical.
dna.was:
74 lines, 60 of them a fallback plane nobody has ever seen -- a 200 m quad grid with two sin/cos hills, reached only when the local rendering device or the SPIR-V load fails. Zero @export of its own, an apply_grid_config whose whole body was `pass` (a method that existed only so the grid's has_method() check would find it), and one real argument sitting as a literal inside MarchingCubesFlat.glsl. The audit recorded the artifact as axis-less, which is true and is not the same as having no parameters.

THE SHADER BUILDS ITS DENSITY IN TWO HALVES THAT DISAGREE ABOUT WHAT KIND OF OBJECT THIS IS. `terrainDensity = (surfaceHeight - worldPos.y) / 30.0` at :189 is a HEIGHTFIELD: a function of x and z, a graph over the plane, single-valued in y everywhere, the one shape you do not need marching cubes for at all -- a quad grid draws it. Then `float density = terrainDensity - (caveNoise * 0.4);` at :193 subtracts four octaves of ridged 3D noise, and at that moment the surface stops being a graph. The whole difference between a plot and a level set is that one literal, in a sequence whose truth line is 'define a field, extract a surface'.
dna.note:
interior is SHARED, taken from csg_architecture_cavity (boolean_surfaces.json, rungs none|corner|court|room), where it asks whether a solid encloses a void you could occupy. Same question asked of a sampled field instead of a boolean solid, and the shared rung `none` means the same thing in both places -- no interior anywhere. Taking it rather than coining `hollowing` is the check as much as the economy: when a shared word is honest the siblings should measure ALIKE, so a landscape's cave and a wall's court clearing the 3% decoration floor at comparable numbers is itself evidence the word is doing one job. NOT `openwork` (csg_architecture_cavity's other axis, about holes in a face). NOT `resolution`, which this sequence already holds twice -- queer_marching_cave and animated_noise_explorer -- with a different question: how finely the field is SAMPLED, not how much of it is subtracted.

EVERY RUNG WAS SIZED ON A FLOAT32 NUMPY REPLICA of evaluate() over the same 65^3 corner grid at the scene's own iso_level of 0.0, counting columns whose solid/air classification changes more than once down y -- which is exactly the question 'is this still a graph over the plane?' -- with triangle counts taken from the shader's own lengths[256] table:

  rung       k     triangles   columns with an inside   enclosed air cells
  none      0.0       12,824        0 of 4,225 (0.00%)                   0
  undercut  0.3       14,996        8 of 4,225 (0.19%)                   9
  caverned  0.4       16,382       50 of 4,225 (1.18%)                  68
  warren    0.8       24,656      436 of 4,225 (10.32%)             1,157

THE MOST INTERESTING THING THIS PROMOTION FOUND is in the third row. The artifact that has stood in ISO_FlatTerrain all along is 98.8% HEIGHTFIELD -- it has an inside in one column in eighty-five. Nobody knew that, because until now there was nothing to compare it against. `none` is the comparison, and it is the picture nobody in this corpus has seen: the exact heightfield y = surfaceHeight, rolling hills from two snoise reads at :182-183 (amplitudes 15.0 and 5.0), smooth, single-sheeted, no overhang ANYWHERE (0 columns, measured, not assumed), marching cubes reduced to a function plotter. It is the negative half of the sequence's claim: here is what the algorithm looks like when it is not being used.

THE APPROVED DESIGN SAID undercut = 0.2 AND THE REPLICA FALSIFIED IT, which is the one place this promotion departs from its brief. At 0.2, ZERO of the 4,225 columns cross more than once and not one air cell is enclosed: 0.2 is a heightfield with its mass thinned, not an undercut. The design defined the rung as 'the first rung where the ground stops being single-valued in y', so declaring 0.2 would have put a word in the registry that the render does not contain -- the science_screen disease in a new costume, and one that no gate could catch because the enum would still match the code. Scanned: the property first appears at 0.25 (one column) and is robust by 0.30. The design's NUMBER and the design's DEFINITION were in conflict; the definition is what the axis argues, so the definition won. 0.30 also lifts the closest pair from a predicted 4.75% focus (under the critic's 6% twin bar) to 8.55%.

warren at 0.8 is void-dominated RELATIVE TO THE REST -- 10.3% of columns, an order of magnitude past the shipped rung, and the only value whose mesh AABB grows (126.6 m tall against 37-56 m) because its caves reach far below the surface band. Not yet floating islands; that needs k past 1.5, which is outside a ladder whose default has to sit inside it.

THE ARTIFACT NEXT DOOR ASKS A DIFFERENT QUESTION ON THE SAME SUBSTRATE, deliberately. ISO_FlatTerrain places mc_flat_landscape and mc_overhang_landscape in the same room. This shader has exactly ONE 3D term, so the only honest axis over it is HOW MUCH inside; the overhang shader has four, so its axis (`landform`) is WHICH TERMS. Neither had to be watered down to avoid the other.

The overhang term is real (it is what makes the ground not single-valued in y) but at 1000 m across and 14.9 degrees of elevation the overhangs are a texture, not a silhouette. That is the rung the sequence's truth line is about, and it is the only one that clearly bites.

The absolute percentages come from a coarse proxy - the 65^3 corner samples binned into a 480 px orthographic depth image, shaded from the depth gradient, pooled to 160x160 - and the real render has finer geometry, true marching-cubes normals and real lights, so THE SWEEP SHOULD READ HIGHER THAN THESE NUMBERS, NOT LOWER. The four displacement figures in metres are not proxies and should hold. If the sweep reports arched<->compound above 1%, the replica is wrong about where the outcrop term lands and this whole entry should be re-read rather than patched. REACH MEASURED BY READING THE MAPS, not estimated: 23 placements in 11 map files by four paths - a bare cell in ISO_AnimatedNoise and two more in Trial_physarum_isosurfaces, a curation_station roster in Corridor_ISO_AnimatedNoise and another in Curation_Bay_isosurfaces_2, sixteen exhibit_furniture#kind:plinth#size:m#mount:animated_noise_explorer across eight Trial_* museums, and two corridor pairs (voxel_noise_demo-> and mc_terrain_demo->) in Trial_physarum_isosurfaces. Not one of them names an axis key; a bare token builds an empty config dict, and GridInteractablesComponent skips _apply_artifact_config entirely when the dict is empty.
dna.was: A 1 m cube of noise that travels: _process pushed current_offset along animation_path and rebuilt the mesh every 0.15 s, forever, and the whole artifact was that motion. Two things were hidden inside it. The resolution of the sampling was a bare local literal, var resolution = 16, invisible to every map and every inspector although it decides everything about the picture. And the extractor is a STUB - create_marching_cubes_mesh tests whether a cell's eight corners straddle iso_level and then emits all six faces of a full solid cube, with no lookup table, no edge interpolation and no case index - so what has always been on screen is not the surface but the set of cells in which the field changes its mind. apply_grid_config was the single word pass, a config channel wired to nothing.
dna.note: extraction is NEW, and the word is the sequence's own verb - define a field, EXTRACT a surface. It exists because this artifact is the one place in the sequence where the question is not rhetorical: its extractor stopped one step short of the surface and left the intermediate on screen, so the four rungs can walk the whole distance in four pictures, every one of them built from the density_field the loop already computes. the ladder is the DIMENSION OF THE ANSWER - a sample, a point on an edge, a face, a cell. cells = a solid cube per straddling cell, SHIPPED, the crude honest default: a mass where a boundary was promised, 917 cells and 5502 quads. faces = the cell faces the contour actually passes through, kept only where the face's own four lattice corners disagree - a perforated stepped sheet running through the block set, 1940 distinct quads, one lattice dimension closer to the surface. corners = a marker at every lattice point above iso_level, no surface at all, the sampled field itself before any decision, 2272 of 4913 points. crossings = a marker at the linearly interpolated point on every lattice edge whose ends disagree, t = (iso - a) / (b - a), which is the exact set of vertices marching cubes would have produced and this extractor never built, 1024 of them. The ladder is the sequence's truth line in reverse: here is the field, here are the points where it crosses, here are the faces it crosses, here is the mass we settled for. MEASURED, NOT GUESSED, AND THE MEASUREMENT CHANGED THE DESIGN. noise_3d, the straddle test and all four extractors were re-implemented in Python against the shipped .tscn values and rasterised with a z-buffer from the sweep's own standpoint (yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26) at 300x300. Against cells: faces differs in 26.31 percent of the frame, corners in 35.27, crossings in 34.20; corners against crossings, 17.29. Subject share of frame 34.50 / 33.08 / 13.90 / 6.32 percent, so the point clouds really are a dust. WHAT THE MEASUREMENT KILLED: the approved rung for faces was the outer SKIN of the straddling set - a face kept only where its six-neighbour does not also straddle. It rasterises 0.00 percent different from cells. Not small, ZERO: all 3486 faces the skin discards are interior and occluded, so under an opaque material a mass and its own skin are the same photograph, and that rung would have published two identical tiles and been filed INERT for a fact about occlusion. The crossed-face reading is the nearest thing that bites, and it argues something the skin did not - not how much of the mass is drawn, but which lattice element the boundary is recorded on. trace (fourier_transform: samples|stems|ribbon; spring_demo: off|phase|wave) is the nearest relative and was refused because its rungs are a one-dimensional signal plot's vocabulary, which a volume cannot answer. workings (csg_difference_demo: outcome|trace|operands|expression) was refused for a sharper reason: workings asks how much of an operation a demonstration will DISCLOSE, and cells is not a fuller disclosure than crossings - it is a cruder extractor. Different claim, different word. resolution is SHARED, taken from riemann_pump (resolution is HOW FINE THE PARTITION IS, and the partition is that artifact's own subject) and given the same three rung names as queer_marching_cave in this same sequence, deliberately, so the two can be read against each other: there a cell size in metres, here a cell count per axis, both naming the shipped state mid. If a shared vocabulary is honest the two behave alike under it, and that is itself a check on the bench. Measured on the shipped field: coarse = 8 gives 232 straddling cells of 0.125 m, mid = 16 gives 917 of 0.0625 m, fine = 24 gives 2070 of 0.0417 m and about 24800 triangles. Capped at 24 on purpose - 32 is 3678 cells and the rebuild is a triple GDScript loop that also runs every regenerate_interval while animating, so a higher rung buys nothing and risks the watchdog. The argument is that the field is continuous and everything you see is an artefact of a sampling rate nobody was told about: same noise function, same threshold, three different objects. Neither axis re-argues fusion or metaball_count, which raymarched_metaballs, metaballs and implicit_surface_modeling already hold for how much the field merges and how many sources it has.
dna.declined: THE ENTIRE TRAVEL APPARATUS, refused by name and all four for the same reason: animation_speed, regenerate_interval, animation_path and auto_start. This artifact's premise is motion - its own Info label reads Traveling Through 4D Noise - and a rate, an interval and a direction are precisely what one PNG cannot photograph. A sweep over animation_speed would publish frames differing only in where the clock happened to be, which is the info_board fault (six identical tiles from five duration exports) with a moving subject instead of a still one. The standing arrangement offered instead is the promoted pair: the two things that are true of the field whether or not anyone is travelling through it - how finely it is sampled, and what a sample is turned into. The travel was only ever a way of showing that the field extends past the box, and extraction=corners shows the same thing in one frame by drawing the field itself. Also declined: show_wireframe, which is a material flag and not a form, and mesh_color.
dna.fixture_why: There is no RNG here of any kind - noise_3d is three hardcoded trigonometric terms and the file contains no randf, no randi and no FastNoiseLite - so the thing that has to be pinned is THE CLOCK. _process accumulates current_offset every frame and regenerates the mesh every regenerate_interval, which means two tiles captured 1.5 s apart photograph two different fields of the same artifact and the sweep would report the shutter as an axis. auto_start false freezes current_offset at Vector3.ZERO, the t=0 field and the only offset every viewer is guaranteed to have seen. Written as a bare JSON boolean, not the string false, because the sweep assigns fixture values straight onto a typed export before _ready. That pin is only safe because of the lifecycle repair recorded under rebuild_guard: until this pass, auto_start false meant NO MESH AT ALL and the fixture would have scored a blank frame INERT. frame_anchor true adds an invisible layers = 0 box the size of the sampled volume so the camera frames the FIELD rather than the extent of whatever the value being tested happened to build - corners and crossings are point clouds whose reach differs from the cube mass by up to a cell, and resolution moves the outermost block by half a cell. No dna.framing key: the subject is a 1 m cube at the origin and the three Label3D nodes do not count toward a MeshInstance3D-only AABB, so the default 1.0 should be honest - but that is an estimate, not a measurement, and it should be checked against the first sweep.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config was the single word pass. It now writes each key as config_<key> metadata, re-reads the two axes against their allow-lists (an unrecognised value is dropped, not applied - the science_screen failure was a typo nothing refused), and rebuilds ONLY when a signature of every value the build reads has actually moved; a config dict naming none of these axes cannot move it. Deliberately narrow: it still ignores chunk_scale, noise_scale, iso_level and the animation knobs, because widening the channel to honour keys nobody has ever sent would be a behaviour change hiding inside a promotion. TWO STRUCTURAL FINDINGS. First, the lifecycle: generate_chunk was reachable only through start_animation, which _ready called only when auto_start was true, so freezing the clock produced no geometry at all. _ready now builds unconditionally and auto_start governs only whether _process advances the offset - for auto_start true, which is the .tscn's value and every placement's, the end state is identical (one chunk at offset zero, is_animating true). Second, the scriptless root: the .tscn root carries no script, the script sits on the child MeshInstance3D NoiseChunk, and the promotion brief expected that to make the axis unreachable from all 11 maps. READ THE ENGINE, IT DOES NOT. GridInteractablesComponent._apply_artifact_config falls through to _config_holder, a breadth-first search for the first descendant that handles config, which finds NoiseChunk; it sets the metadata there and calls apply_grid_config on it, and all of that happens BEFORE parent_node.add_child, so the child's _ready sees the keys. capture_config_sweep._holder_of does the same for the bench. So no forwarder script was added to the root: the gap the brief describes was closed at the call site, and adding a second handler would only have given the axis two homes. The only node this script creates is the frame anchor and it is tracked in an _owned array - GridInteractablesComponent attaches a _RotationTimer to spawned artifacts, so freeing every child is never safe here.

dna.finding: THIS ARTIFACT DOES NOT EXTRACT AN ISOSURFACE, and the axis only makes sense after that. create_metaball_proxy_mesh builds a SphereMesh of radius 3.0 at 64 radial segments and 32 rings, walks it with a MeshDataTool, and displaces each vertex along its OWN normal by (field_value - surface_threshold) * 0.2 plus a noise wrinkle of 0.1. Its own comment says so: 'a workaround to avoid implementing full marching cubes'. The genus is pinned at 0 by the proxy - this surface can never split, never merge and never open a hole, whatever the field does. The field is a readout painted onto a fixed shape, in a sequence whose truth line is 'the boundary between inside and outside becomes geometry'. Here it does not become geometry; it is projected onto geometry that was already there.
dna.default: imprint=relief. The value is never read from IMPRINT_DEPTH: _imprint_depth() short-circuits on 'relief' and returns the bare literal 0.2, so the shipped path does not depend on the table at all. The two curation_station rosters that name this token (Corridor_ISO_Metaballs, Curation_Bay_isosurfaces_4) pass nothing either.
dna.was: The hardcoded literal 0.2 in the vertex displacement. apply_grid_config was a bare `pass`, so no map could reach any parameter of this artifact.
dna.note: imprint = how deep the summed field is pressed into a surface that was never derived from it. blank 0.0 - the field does not reach the skin at all, leaving a 3 m sphere carrying only the 0.1 wrinkle; the one frame in the corpus showing a metaball artifact's surface with its metaballs REMOVED, and the evidence for the finding above. relief 0.2 shipped. swollen 0.6. flayed 1.2, where the sixty sources push the skin into spikes and the flat annulus they are arranged in becomes legible through it. Deliberately neither taken metaball word: `fusion` is smin(a,b,k) on a raymarched SDF, a blend OPERATOR between distance functions, and this artifact sums rather than blends; `metaball_count` is the number of summands. imprint is a third question only this artifact can ask, because only this artifact has a surface that exists independently of its field. `relief` and `impression` were the better English words for the whole axis and are both taken (push_relabel_algorithm, ten_print_maze_3d), so `relief` survives as the shipped rung.
dna.declined: surface_threshold, AND THIS DECLINE IS THE RESULT OF THE PASS. It is the artifact's own advertised critical_parameter: the @identity block claims 'lower thresholds make the field bleed wider (one creature), higher thresholds reveal individual spheres (many creatures)'. The arithmetic refuses it. In `vertex += normal * (field_value - surface_threshold) * 0.2` the threshold enters only as -T * 0.2 * normal - a constant displacement along each vertex's own outward normal, which on a sphere is exactly a change of RADIUS. Sweeping T gives spheres of different sizes carrying identical lumps, and it can neither separate a body nor merge one because the proxy's genus is fixed. Four tiles, one picture, and the verdict would have been a fact about the registry's prose rather than about the artifact. Filed as a defect in the @identity, not swept. ALSO DECLINED: movement_speed - DEAD CODE, reported and left alone. It is written into each metaball's `velocity` field in create_metaballs and `velocity` is read by nothing; all motion comes from the noise term, the centre attraction and the radius sine in update_metaballs. Wiring it now would change what the one live room draws, so it stays dead and stays documented. num_metaballs (60) is `metaball_count`, taken. container_size, base_radius, radius_variation are a bound and two magnitudes on sources that reach the picture only through imprint. material_color and every shader parameter are chrome.
dna.fixture_why: UNSEEDED TWICE OVER AND ANIMATED. noise.seed was `randi()` - the literal opposite of seeded - and it feeds both the per-vertex wrinkle and the drift. create_metaballs then draws from the GLOBAL RNG SEVEN times per ball (distance, angle, z, radius, and three velocity components) for sixty balls, so five variants would have been five different objects. metaball_seed uses the same sentinel as metaballs.gd: at 0 every draw falls through to the global randf_range/randi in the identical order, so the one placement is untouched; non-zero routes every draw through a local RandomNumberGenerator seeded before the first sample, noise.seed included. POSE: _process advances time, moves the sources and calls generate_mesh() every frame - a full MeshDataTool rebuild of a 64x32 sphere per frame. pose_time below zero keeps the shipped wall clock. Zero or above cannot be a closed form, because update_metaballs early-returns on even Engine.get_frames_drawn() and advances only thirty of the sixty balls per call from a start index derived from time, so the state at t is a function of how many discrete update calls happened. pose_time >= 0.0 is therefore DEFINED as: run round(pose_time * 60) fixed 1/60 s steps synchronously inside _ready, replaying the every-other-frame parity on the virtual step index, then build once and set_process(false). That reproduces the DENSITY of updates, not any particular live frame - the real frame counter's value at spawn is arbitrary, which is exactly why the pose has to be pinned rather than sampled.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config returns immediately on an empty dictionary, then takes each of imprint / metaball_seed / pose_time only when it validates AND differs from the current value, and calls _rebuild() only if something changed and _ready has already built once (_built). All three placement sites pass no keys at all, so they reach no assignment and never rebuild. _rebuild frees nothing - the body is one MeshInstance3D and three lights, all reused - and the nodes this script creates are tracked in an _owned array that is the only thing _exit_tree touches.

So blank is 6.2 across, relief 7.24, swollen 9.32, flayed 12.44. dna.predicted_degeneracy:
inverse_square x wyvill, and this CORRECTS the approved design, which named inverse_square x gaussian. Solve each kernel for the distance at which ONE mean source (strength 0.85, radius 0.45, so strength*radius^2 = 0.1721) alone reaches iso 0.65, and you get the radius of an isolated ball: inverse_square 0.1721/d^2 = 0.65 -> d = 0.515 m; wyvill 0.85(1 - d^2/3.24)^3 = 0.65 -> d = 0.526 m; cone 0.85(1 - d/1.8) = 0.65 -> d = 0.424 m; gaussian 0.85exp(-d^2/0.405) = 0.65 -> d = 0.330 m. inverse_square and wyvill are 2.2% apart and every other pair is 20-36% apart, so gaussian is the FARTHEST rung from the default, not the nearest. The design read long-tailed as similar, and the tail is not what sets the ball.

What separates the close pair is therefore not the ball but the BACKGROUND. At emplacement=column ten sources span about 6 m; under inverse_square a point 1.5 m from the nearest still collects 0.0765 from it and roughly 0.15 more from the other eight, so the local iso is effectively 0.65 - 0.20 = 0.45 and the column's radius solves to 0.618 m. Under wyvill everything past R = 4 x radius = 1.8 m is exactly zero, so the same column stands at 0.526 m. A 17% radius change on a tall thin body: PREDICTED 5% of frame, 9% focus. If it lands under 3% the honest reading is that a 17% waist on a subject occupying a narrow vertical strip is simply not enough pixels, and the crop (framing 0.85) is the first thing to check - not the axis.

SECOND PREDICTION, crossed, and the one worth the pass because it can fail loudly. At emplacement=shell the ten sources sit on a Fibonacci sphere of radius min(bounds)*0.7 = 1.575 m. The field AT THE CENTRE is 10 x 0.1721/2.4806 = 0.694 under inverse_square against iso 0.65 - a 6.8% margin, so the bag is SOLID - and 10 x 0.85(1 - 2.4806/3.24)^3 = 0.110 under wyvill, so it is HOLLOW. That is a real difference in the field and the camera CANNOT SEE IT, because the bag is closed either way and from outside both are a ~3.6 m sphere. It is written here so that a small number on shell x kernel is read as the closed surface it is and not as a dead axis. The rung where kernel is loudest is scatter, not shell: uniform in a 4.5 x 9.6 x 4.5 m box the mean nearest-neighbour spacing is about 1.49 m, and at the midpoint gaussian gives 2 x 0.85exp(-0.555/0.405) = 0.43 (BELOW iso, ten separate beads) where inverse_square gives 0.62 plus tails = 0.77 and wyvill 0.97 (both connected).
dna.default:
emplacement=column AND kernel=inverse_square, and both are SHORT-CIRCUITS rather than table entries that happen to land on the shipped number. _emplace() at column evaluates the same three expressions the loop always evaluated, in the same order, drawing from the same stream: _jitter(null, bounds.x * 0.3) is randf_range(-half, half) where -half is an exact IEEE sign flip of the identical product, then bounds.y * y_frac * 0.7 with no draw, then the z jitter. Strength and radius follow, then Metaball._init's six animation draws with rng == null - the shipped global calls, unchanged. And inverse_square is not a kernel branch inside the hot loop but its OWN triple loop: the same load and the same divide, mb_sr2[m] / dist_sq, because a general kernel evaluated at the parameters that reproduce an inverse square is not the same instruction stream as an inverse square.

dna.note:
emplacement is WHERE THE FIELD'S SOURCES STAND, which is the half of the metaball question metaballs.tscn does not ask. That artifact owns metaball_count (how many sources) and fusion (how hard they blend), and both bite at 53% and 74%. This one holds the count at the scene's own 10 on every single rung - same summands, same kernel, same iso - and moves only the geometry of provenance, so the sweep demonstrates that where is independent of how many. column = SHIPPED, a stack from -3.36 m to +2.69 m with +/-0.675 m of jitter. ring = a circle of radius bounds.x * 0.6 = 1.35 m in XZ at y = 0; neighbours land ~0.85 m apart, inside every kernel here, so the extraction closes into a torus rather than into ten beads. pair = two clusters at +/- bounds.y * 0.6, 5.76 m centre to centre, the count split evenly, with a 0.72 m vertical spread inside each cluster so the five members merge into one body and the two bodies do not - the arrangement in which a FIXED threshold decides whether this artifact is one thing or two. shell = a Fibonacci sphere at min(bounds) * 0.7 = 1.575 m, sources on a hollow. scatter = uniform through the whole volume, against column's 0.3 of it.

kernel is WHAT ONE SOURCE CONTRIBUTES, and the relation to the taken word is said out loud rather than left for the critic. fusion on metaballs.tscn is smin(a, b, k), a smooth-minimum BLEND between two signed distance functions in a raymarcher that never sums anything. kernel is the falloff of the summands in a potential field that IS summed, on a 30 x 64 x 30 scalar grid that IS marched. One is an operator between distance functions; the other is the function being added. They will still produce related silhouettes at their extremes - gaussian on a wide scatter looks like fusion=distinct - and the reason is not that the axes are the same question but that a tight kernel and a disengaged smin both refuse to join two bodies. falloff was the natural word and is taken by wave_propagation_3d.

inverse_square = SHIPPED: strength * radius^2 / d^2, INFINITE SUPPORT, which the code then truncates at 5% of iso to afford it. That truncation is the artifact admitting what its field is made of, and it is why this axis exists at all. wyvill = s(1 - d^2/R^2)^3 for d < R with R = 4 x radius, exactly zero beyond - the only rung on which the cull is not an approximation but the kernel's own edge, so _update_influence_radii returns R itself there rather than a solved tail. gaussian = s exp(-d^2/2r^2), smooth, long-tailed, and by the arithmetic in predicted_degeneracy the TIGHTEST ball of the four. cone = s max(0, 1 - d/R), only C0, so the summed field creases where two sources meet and the extracted surface carries the crease.

EVERY TILE THEREFORE DIFFERS IN FULL-FRAME SURFACE COLOUR AND ALPHA FOR REASONS THAT BELONG TO NEITHER AXIS.
