Same question, two ontologies of showing. margin is a NEW word, and it is the sequence's truth line - 'define a field, extract a surface' - turned into a knob. The demo hardcodes 0.3 for outside and 0.7 for inside against MarchingCubesGenerator's threshold of 0.5. That pair is SYMMETRIC about the threshold, so every interpolated vertex lands on the exact edge midpoint: the diagram-book picture, and an accident of two literals rather than a property of the algorithm. Slide the pair while keeping its span at 0.4 and the fifteen cases stay the same fifteen cases - same config bytes, same table entries, same topology, the same eight beads in the same eight colours in the same eight places - while every sheet slides across its cell. The table decides what the surface IS; the numbers decide where it SITS; and only one of those is in the lookup table. Values are (outside, inside) pairs and t is measured from the inside corner: even (0.30, 0.70) t=0.50 SHIPPED; starved (0.14, 0.54) t=0.10, the inside corners barely made it and the sheets hug them until the solid is slivers; swollen (0.44, 0.84) t=0.85, the sheets stand off toward the outside corners and the solid nearly fills its cell; brimming (0.48, 0.88) t=0.95, the limit case. Words considered and rejected for this axis, each because it already carries a different claim elsewhere: `bias` (pixel_cloud), `crossing` (sine_space, sine_space_explanation, fluency_seam), and `reading`. margin names the quantity actually being varied - the distance of each sample from the threshold. rhizome_cave_demo.qfep_connection: A cave grown as rhizome — Deleuze's centerless, multiply-connected figure carved into stone by branching growth and marching cubes. The post-crisis answer in geology: after the foundations fell, you build spaces with no single entrance and no privileged path, structures that are all middle. A world you enter anywhere and cross more than one way — formalization's limits turned into an architecture of the between.

dna.note:
strata is a NEW word and the nearest taken relatives were each refused for a reason. `landform` (mc_overhang_landscape) and `interior` (mc_flat_landscape) name what a field PRODUCES; strata names which summands it is BUILT FROM. `octaves` (mc_cave, mc_inside_cave) is how many scales of ONE noise survive; this is which of THREE DIFFERENT noises contributes at all. `admixture` and `fusion` are held elsewhere in this same sequence with the sense of blending one field into another, which is a smooth knob; strata is a switchboard.

THE RUNGS, and the arithmetic that sizes them. calculate_terrain_density sums three noises into one height: height_noise (TYPE_PERLIN, frequency 0.05, 4 octaves, gain 0.5, lacunarity 2.0, weight 1.0), detail_noise (TYPE_SIMPLEX, frequency 0.15, 2 octaves, weight 0.2) and feature_noise (TYPE_CELLULAR, RETURN_CELL_VALUE, frequency 0.015, weight 0.3). The axis multiplies those three weights and touches nothing else. all = SHIPPED (1.0, 0.2, 0.3). bedrock = (1, 0, 0), the pure fBm ground with no cells and no crust. cells = (0, 0, 1), cellular alone. fine = (0, 1, 0), simplex alone. The sole-layer rungs carry weight 1.0 rather than the shipped 0.3 and 0.2 so each shows its layer at full strength, which makes `all` about 1.5x the amplitude of a sole rung - stated rather than hidden, and the reason swell is crossed with it.

AND THEN THE FOOTPRINT ARITHMETIC, WHICH IS THE FINDING OF THIS PASS. The controller sets terrain_size 10 against a chunk of 16 x 0.8 = 12.8 m, so the grid is exactly ONE chunk and the whole artifact is 12.8 m across. Measure each layer's feature size against that: Perlin at 0.05 has a 20 m base period, so the footprint is 0.64 of one period plus its 10 / 5 / 2.5 m octaves - a broad ramp with wiggles, which is the picture everyone has seen. Simplex at 0.15 gives 6.7 m and 3.3 m features - about two bumps across the footprint, genuinely the finest of the three. Cellular at 0.015 has a lattice spacing of 66.7 m. THE FOOTPRINT IS 0.19 OF ONE VORONOI CELL. RETURN_CELL_VALUE is constant per cell, so at this artifact's own scale the third summand is not a layer of features at all - it is a single number, a DC offset of up to +/-0.6 m on the shipped weight. That is why `cells` is predicted to photograph as one perfectly flat plate (see predicted_degeneracy), and it is a better answer to `what is the field made of` than a prettier rung would have been: one third of this field is a constant.

swell is also NEW. `relief` was the natural word and is taken once by push_relabel_algorithm, where it means the graph algorithm's relabel operation - an unrelated question, so reusing it would confuse rather than build a family. Not `bulge` (queer_marching_cave), which is a local swelling of a cave wall rather than the global amplitude of a height field. The literal is terrain_height = 5.0, declared twice (TerrainGenerator:21 and TerrainDemoController:30) and reaching the field through update_terrain_parameters()'s "height" key; it scales the entire noise sum and nothing else.

THE LADDER DOES NOT REACH ZERO, and the approved design asked that it should - `plane = 0.0`, a perfectly flat slab, offered as the evidence for the defect below. IT RENDERS NOTHING, and the arithmetic is short. Chunks are created at y = 0.0 (create_terrain_voxel_grid:169) and sampled upward for 12 x 0.8 = 9.6 m, so the box floor IS the mean plane. The density ladder lerps 0.45 -> 0.75 across the unit below the surface and therefore crosses iso 0.5 at surface_factor 1/6, i.e. 0.167 units BELOW the geometric surface. At amplitude 0 the extracted surface sits at y = -0.167, outside the sampled column; every voxel in the box reads 0.45 or less; marching cubes finds no crossing anywhere and the tile is empty. Nor can a small amplitude stand in for it: LOW AMPLITUDE RENDERS LESS, NOT FLATTER, because only the fraction of the footprint where combined_height clears 0.167 gets any geometry at all. So the rungs go UP from the default instead of down to zero: rolling = 5.0 SHIPPED, subdued = 2.5, hills = 9.0, range = 13.0. CEILING ARITHMETIC, do not overshoot: at 13.0 the crest is max_sum x 13 x 0.4, and `all` has a maximum sum near 1.5, so 7.8 m - still inside the 9.6 m column. Above about 15 the terrain leaves the chunk and the rung photographs as holes rather than as mountains.
dna.declined:
REFUSED, surface_threshold (0.5): `threshold` is taken by mc_torus_sculpture, and here it would also be degenerate - calculate_terrain_density is monotone in distance_to_surface, so a constant threshold offset is exactly a vertical translation of the extracted surface and would argue with swell for the same pixels. REFUSED, debug_disable_surface_variation and debug_minimum_density: the controller hardcodes debug_mode true and min_density 0.7, so surface_var is permanently 0.0; switching it on adds detail_value * 0.05 = +/-0.01 into a band 0.30 wide, a 3.3% perturbation of the transition zone, below the bite floor - and two values is below the axis floor anyway. REFUSED, noise_frequency (0.05): a real field property, but the same ratio question as `resolution`, already used twice in this sequence. REFUSED, chunk_size and voxel_scale: the sampling lattice, i.e. resolution again. REFUSED, terrain_size, the chunk material and the wireframe flag: a footprint and chrome.

FOUR THINGS REPORTED AS DEFECTS RATHER THAN SWEPT.

1. THE HEADLINE: THIS ARTIFACT'S FIELD IS TWO-DIMENSIONAL. All three layers are sampled with get_noise_2d(world_pos.x, world_pos.z) and the density is a five-branch piecewise ramp in world_pos.y minus that height. Density is monotone decreasing in y at every column, so there is exactly one crossing per column: the field is a height function extruded, and it cannot produce an overhang, a cave, a bridge or a disconnected body - the entire subject of the sequence it sits in. Its own registry description promises 'configurable noise parameters'; what it cannot do is the thing marching cubes is for.

2. THE LADDER DOES NOT CROSS ITS OWN THRESHOLD AT THE SURFACE. lerp(0.45, 0.75, surface_factor) = 0.5 at surface_factor = 1/6, so the extracted iso-surface sits 0.167 units BELOW the geometric one everywhere. (The approved design put this at 0.833, which is 1 - 1/6 - the complement, not the offset.) Combined with a chunk floor at y = 0 this is why roughly half the footprint carries no geometry at the shipped settings: wherever combined_height < 0.167 the whole column is air. The shipped picture is a partial sheet, not a ground.

3. A 73.36 m DECORATIVE PLANE, 5.7x THE ARTIFACT. marching_cubes_terrain_demo.tscn carries a MeshInstance3D with a PlaneMesh at scale 36.68 and a translucent pink material, sitting at y = -0.1. The terrain is 12.8 m. That plane is the entire content of this registry's `measurements.aabb_size` of [73.36, 0.89, 73.36] and of both entries' footprint_measured of 74 x 74 cells - a spatial contract, a placement footprint and a capture framing all sized to a backdrop rather than to the artifact. It is left in place (it ships in all five placements and defaults are sacred) and dna.framing is set against it instead; see framing_why.

4. A LEAK ON EVERY GENERATION. TerrainGenerator.generate_walkable_collision allocates a bare `Node3D` as temp_parent, parents the navigation tiles and the VR teleport markers to it, and frees it only on its two early-return branches. On the success path it is never freed and never enters the tree, so every regeneration strands a Node3D and its tile children. Not touched here: fixing it changes the shipped path, and this pass owes those five placements a bit-identical build.

dna.predicted_degeneracy:
TWO PREDICTIONS, and the second one is the interesting one because it predicts a DEFECT.

strata, PREDICTED CLOSEST PAIR: all x bedrock, predicted ~7% focus. They differ by exactly (0.2 * detail + 0.3 * feature) * terrain_height * 0.4 = (0.2 d + 0.3 f) * 2.0 at swell=rolling. The cellular term f is a CONSTANT across this footprint (see note - 0.19 of one Voronoi cell), so 0.3 f * 2.0 is a pure vertical offset of up to +/-0.6 m that moves no silhouette at all, and what is actually left between the two frames is 0.2 d * 2.0 = +/-0.4 m of simplex ripple on a sheet whose whole relief is about 1.5 m. That is 27% of the relief but it lives in shading rather than in outline. If it comes back under 3% the two tiles are photographs of the same Perlin ridge and the honest reading is that two of this artifact's three layers are decoration at its own scale.

swell, PREDICTED CLOSEST PAIR: rolling x subdued, predicted ~6% focus. Note this is NOT the pair with the smallest ratio - hills:range is 1.44 against rolling:subdued's 2.0 - because the camera is pinned by one union AABB and does not retreat, so what the frame sees is the ABSOLUTE difference in relief: rolling minus subdued is 2.5 * 0.4 * max_sum ~ 0.75 m, while hills minus range is 4.0 * 0.4 * max_sum ~ 1.2 m. The low rung also loses coverage - the fraction of the footprint clearing the 0.167 iso offset drops from about 45% to about 30% - so if subdued measures LARGER than predicted, the axis is being read as coverage rather than as relief, and that is a true statement about the artifact rather than an error.

dna.note: WHERE THIS ARTIFACT'S FIELD COMES FROM, which is what wave 3 of the isosurfaces sequence is asking. Nowhere else in the sequence is the answer 'from a history'. Every other member samples a function at each lattice point — a gyroid, a noise, a sum of metaball kernels. This one evaluates nothing: generate_cave_async fills the whole chunk with density 1.0 (:346-349) and then SUBTRACTS, carve_sphere writing min(current, dist/voxel_radius) (:265) along a graph that grew iteration by iteration out of an RNG. Both axes are lifted out of that record, one from the growth and one from the carve, and they are orthogonal by construction: anastomosis decides the graph and never touches a radius; bore scales the radius and cannot reach the graph, because the graph is finished before the first voxel is written. ANASTOMOSIS asks whether a branch that meets an existing one rejoins it or stops. RhizomeGrowthPattern.find_merge_candidate (:171-176) returns the first existing node within merge_distance of a proposed branch tip; on a hit create_connection adds an EDGE and `continue` suppresses the new node, which is the only way a circuit can enter this graph. tree=0.0: nothing is ever within 0 m, so nothing ever merges — a pure arborescence with dead ends and no circuit, the figure Deleuze and Guattari oppose and the thing this artifact's own truth statement claims to refute, rendered here for the first time. netted=6.0 SHIPPED. matted=12.0. knotted=20.0. THE CONFOUND, stated rather than hidden: raising merge_distance both adds edges and SUPPRESSES nodes, because the merging branch does not create the node it was going to create. The network gets loopier and smaller at the same time and no still can separate the two. BORE asks how wide the same graph is carved. The multiplier lives inside carve_sphere, the single gate every carve passes through (carve_tunnel reaches the field only by calling it), so the graph is bit-for-bit identical across all four rungs — same seed, same nodes, same positions, same rng draws. At thread the carve radius is 1.2 m against a 1.0 m voxel and the solid boundary sits at 0.6 of a voxel, so the tube is thinner than the sampling lattice and a continuous field extracts as a broken string of beads; at hollow the tubes swallow each other and the surface merges what the graph deliberately kept apart. The fixture uses 3.0..26.0, which measures 0 / 34 / 59 / 89 percent merged and 175 / 65 / 18 / 3 nodes: four different graphs, monotone, none degenerate.
